briefing.text: Before considering 'Not verifiable', check whether data_clinical_sample.txt holds a per-sample TMB variable (e.g. TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS, nonsynonymous mutations per Mb) and what CANCER_TYPE the samples are. If a TMB variable exists and the cohort is cervical cancer, the hypothesis is about this study and the benchmark convention calls for True or False, decided from the TMB counts.
briefing.reason: Calling a testable hypothesis 'Not verifiable' is graded as wrong, and the main risk is missing that the TMB column is there.

briefing.text: Use the provided per-Mb TMB column as the main evidence. If you recompute TMB from data_mutations.txt, count only nonsynonymous coding mutations and divide each sample by the size of its own gene panel (data_gene_panel_matrix.txt; MSK-IMPACT panels are about 0.98 Mb for IMPACT341, 1.06 Mb for IMPACT410 and 1.14 Mb for IMPACT468). Do not use an exome-size denominator or a single panel size for every sample. Compare the result with the provided column.
briefing.reason: A wrong denominator, or counting silent and intronic variants, shifts TMB values across the 10 mut/Mb cutoff.

briefing.text: Report counts at both TMB >10 and TMB >=10 mut/Mb, since samples on the borderline can change the count. Check CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED and ONCOTREE_CODE for any TMB-high samples so that you know they are cervical tumours, and break the counts down by histology.
briefing.reason: The hypothesis uses a strict threshold, and every TMB-high sample has to be a cervical cancer before it counts.

briefing.text: The hypothesis is about patients, not samples. Check for patients with more than one sample (e.g. primary plus metastasis), and give results at patient level (per-patient max, or one sample per patient) as well as at sample level.
briefing.reason: Repeated samples from one patient inflate the count of TMB-high cases.

briefing.text: For any TMB-high sample, look at MSI_TYPE/MSI_SCORE, POLE and mismatch-repair gene mutations (MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2), TUMOR_PURITY, SAMPLE_COVERAGE and SOMATIC_STATUS (Matched vs Unmatched). Hypermutation explained by MSI/MMR deficiency, POLE or APOBEC is real biology, not an artefact; cervical cancer is known to include hypermutated, APOBEC-high tumours (TCGA 2017). Exclude a sample only for a clear QC failure. Unmatched (tumour-only) samples can have inflated TMB from germline variants, and low purity or coverage lowers TMB, so report these as sensitivity checks.
briefing.reason: It shows which high-TMB values are trustworthy and stops teams from discarding real outliers or relying on artefactual ones.

shared_assumptions: Both teams treat the deposited TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS column as the TMB the hypothesis refers to (panel-based nonsynonymous mutations per Mb), on the same scale as the 10 mut/Mb threshold.
Both treat every sample in the table as a cervical cancer patient in scope, including metastasis samples and rare histologies (e.g. gastric-type mucinous, neuroendocrine).
unused_evidence: SAMPLE_TYPE (Primary vs Metastasis): neither team reported whether TMB-high cases are confined to metastatic or pretreated samples; this cannot remove them from 'cervical cancer patients' but would describe them.
data_cna, data_cna_hg19.seg and data_sv were not used; they are irrelevant to a TMB existence claim and cannot change the count.
unresolved_weak_points: Both named approximate panel Mb denominators as weakest point; this is resolved in practice because the deposited TMB column agrees with the recount (r=0.999) and 22 of 177 patients exceed 10.
Team A reported 4 TMB-high samples with MSI_TYPE 'Do not report' and low purity; low purity would bias TMB downward, so this does not threaten the count.
second_readings: 'Not present in any cervical cancer patients' could be read as 'TMB-high is not a feature of cervical cancer in general'; under either reading, 22/177 (~12%) patients above 10 mut/Mb contradicts it. No reading on another scale or time point changes the conclusion.
challenge.verdict: High trust in the agreed 'False': both teams found 22 of 177 cervical cancer patients with deposited TMB >10, confirmed by independent recount, all matched-normal, and TMB-high cervical cancer is established biology; the only questions are descriptive robustness checks.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Break the 22 TMB>10 patients down by SAMPLE_TYPE (Primary vs Metastasis) and by CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED, and check how many remain if you keep only primary squamous/adeno cervical tumours; does any plausible restriction bring the count to zero and so change the method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: For the 22 TMB>10 samples, list SOMATIC_STATUS, TUMOR_PURITY and SAMPLE_COVERAGE and check whether any is Unmatched or low coverage (possible germline inflation); does the count of clearly valid TMB-high cases stay above zero, and does that change your method?
